rationale: A selector-chain term is resolved by a published name of the SAME selector kind. `real-css-analyzer.ts`'s `resolves()` had four sub-tests — exact name, dotted LEAF, any `:`/`.` boundary TAIL — and the last two did not compare kinds, so the TYPE-selector rule `button` satisfied the CLASS term `.button`. Measured on the corpus (single-file-dump.ts): geb/doc/site/public/css/semantic.min.css emits `contains ".button" -> ".button"` with names.has(".button") = false and names.has("button") = true. The forbids below are that defect at fixture scale; the one expect row is the control that proves chains are still emitted when both terms ARE published.

forbidRelationships.comment: the class term `.button` is satisfied only by the TYPE rule `button`
the same defect on a mixed-kind compound: `button.button` is not a declared selector

_targetSpelling: CSS-D15: a target that names a declaration THIS file publishes is spelled `<file-scope>::<name>`, where the scope is the file's project-relative path without its extension. The bare spelling stays for a target this file does not declare (a cross-file or external reference) and for `imports`, whose target is another file's module name.
